prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but first a few quick points so my recommendations are useful:

- Do you want a short list of specific attorneys/firms in Pleasanton/Alameda County for me to evaluate? I can’t browse the web in real time, but I can help you evaluate names you give or show you exactly how to find and compare good local lawyers.
- Tell me a bit about the crash/injury (severity, who was at fault, whether you’ve talked to insurers, whether you’ve seen a doctor). That will change which lawyer is best (minor soft-tissue claim vs. catastrophic injury or permanent disability).

Meanwhile, here’s practical, immediate guidance so you can find and hire the right car-accident lawyer.

Immediate steps (do these now if you haven’t):
- Get medical care and follow treatment. Document everything (dates, diagnoses, bills).
- Preserve evidence: photos of vehicles, scene, injuries; police report; witness names/contact info; repair estimates.
- Do not sign any full release or give a recorded statement to an insurance company without advice from an attorney.
- Note deadlines: California’s personal injury statute of limitations is typically 2 years from the injury (Cal. Code Civ. Proc. §335.1). Claims against government entities have much shorter deadlines (often 6 months). If a government vehicle or agency is involved, act quickly.

How to choose the right lawyer
Look for these core qualifications and qualities:
- Experience with car-accident personal injury claims (not only traffic tickets or DUI defense).
- Trial experience and willingness to go to trial if necessary (many firms settle most cases; defense insurers test plaintiffs they believe won’t go to trial).
- Local court experience in Alameda County and familiarity with local judges, opposing counsel, and local medical-legal experts.
- Track record of settlements/verdicts in cases similar to yours (ask for dollar ranges).
- Clear fee structure (contingency fee percentage, who advances costs, what happens if you settle before/after filing suit).
- Good communication: prompt responses, clear point of contact, and realistic expectations.
- Resources to hire experts (medical experts, accident reconstruction) if your case needs them.
- Good reviews/references and no serious disciplinary history (check the State Bar).

What to expect on fees and costs
- Most personal injury lawyers take cases on contingency (no fee unless you recover money). Typical contingency ranges:
  - ~33% if settled before filing suit
  - ~33–40% if suit is filed and case goes through trial/appeal
- You’ll often be responsible for case costs (filing fees, expert fees) which the attorney typically advances and is reimbursed from recovery.
- Confirm exactly when fees are taken and how costs are handled in writing.

Questions to ask at the initial (usually free) consultation
- Do you handle car-accident injury cases? How long have you been handling them?
- How many cases like mine have you handled and what were typical outcomes?
- Will you personally handle my case or will associates/ paralegals do most of the work?
- Do you have trial experience in Alameda County? How often do you take cases to trial?
- What contingency fee do you charge? What costs will I be responsible for if we don’t win?
- How long do you expect this case would take to resolve?
- How do you communicate with clients (phone, email, how often)? Who is my main point of contact?
- Can you provide references from former clients (or examples of anonymized settlements/verdicts)?
- Any conflicts of interest with any of the parties or insurers?

Red flags to avoid
- Guarantees of a specific settlement amount.
- Unwillingness to put fee agreement in writing.
- High-pressure tactics to sign immediately.
- Difficult or evasive answers about trial history or who will handle the case day-to-day.
- Poor client communication during the consult (unreturned calls, rude staff).

Where to find local lawyers
- Alameda County Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service or local bar referral.
- State Bar of California “Find a Lawyer” to check standing and specialties.
- Online review sites (Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Yelp) — use reviews as one input, not the only one.
- Ask trusted friends, family, or medical providers for referrals.
- If the case is serious (catastrophic injury, permanent disability), consider firms that focus on complex injury litigation and have experience with high-value cases.

What to bring to a consultation
- Police report (if available) or collision report number
- Photos of scene, vehicles, injuries
- Medical records and bills, or at least dates/locations of treatment
- Insurance information for you and the other driver(s)
- Any correspondence from insurers
- Names/contact info for witnesses
- Repair estimates or vehicle valuations

If you want, I can:
- Provide a short checklist/template to compare 3–5 lawyers after you have consultations.
- Evaluate specific attorney/firms if you give me their names and any info you find (reviews, verdicts).
- Draft a list of tailored questions based on the injuries and facts you provide.

Tell me whether you’d like help finding names of Pleasanton or Alameda County attorneys to contact, or paste a few attorney names you’re considering and I’ll help you evaluate them.
